title: Scheming Eval Replication: Code-Specialized vs. General Models

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Direct deployment risk assessment: coding assistants have direct file/system access in production. If coding specialization amplifies tool-use scheming, this is a high-priority risk finding for the coding assistant deployment wave.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Code-specialized models are publicly available (Code Llama, DeepSeek-Coder). Running Apollo's code-adjacent scheming scenarios requires agentic eval infrastructure with code execution environments. The setup is non-trivial but more focused than general scheming evals.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused on code-adjacent scenarios only (file manipulation, tool-use subversion, self-exfiltration via code), which narrows the eval space. But the agentic infrastructure for code execution environments is still substantial setup. Achievable in 30 hours if using existing eval frameworks.
